instructions: Review every checkpoint in every scenario in order. Treat each checkpoint as a rendered user-visible state, not as a representative sample. For each action, compare the before and after screenshot and accessibility tree with the declared action, phase, expected identifiers, expected labels, and invariant names. Setup failures are blocked evidence and must not be reported as product defects. Assertion failures are product evidence and a declared checkpoint outcome of fail makes the acceptance run fail. Missing contracts or incomplete artifacts are unverified or blocked and cannot be called a pass. Inspect functionality, visual hierarchy, layout, copy, affordances, accessibility, touch targets, persistence signals, performance symptoms, transitions, loading and error states, and anything a human user would find confusing or suspicious. Use automated tree-lint findings as evidence: trust touch-target findings only when the captured element state says it is existing, enabled, and hittable; use the breadcrumb to locate anonymous controls; and treat symbol/repeated-row duplicate suppression as intentional lint policy. Then apply human judgment to the remaining visual and experience questions. Report only observable issues, name the first divergent checkpoint, distinguish confirmed failures from suspects and environmental blockers, and return one JSON object matching responseSchema.

findings.category: functionality | visual | accessibility | copy | interaction | persistence | performance | privacy | watch-sync | reliability
